title: What If Every Human Vanished Tomorrow?

youtube.title: What If Every Human Vanished Tomorrow? | Dig Deeper
youtube.description: What would happen if every human disappeared tomorrow? Sir Digsworth follows the real expert timeline: the lights going out within hours, New York's subway flooding in about 36 hours, animals taking over our cities, roads turning into forests, and the human-made things that could last for millions of years.

scenes.narration: Imagine waking up tomorrow, and every other human on Earth is simply gone.
Good morning, I'm Sir Digsworth. Experts have actually studied what would happen next, and the timeline is wild. The strangest part comes at the very end, so do stay with me.
Within hours, the lights begin to go out. Most power plants burn fuel, and with nobody delivering more, one by one they shut down.
Experts estimate that within a few weeks, the whole planet goes dark at night. No street lights. No glowing windows. Nothing.
Meanwhile, beneath New York, more than seven hundred pumps normally keep the subway dry. Without power, the tunnels fill with water in about thirty six hours.

fact.label: Did you know?
fact.text: New York's subway pumps remove about 13 million gallons of water every day.

scenes.narration: After about ten days, the food in shops and fridges starts to rot. Smells lovely, I'm sure.
Some animals would do just fine without us. Pigs, for example, go wild surprisingly fast.
Raccoons, rats and pigeons would move straight into our empty buildings. Rent free, of course.
And with no city lights at all, the Milky Way would blaze across the sky, even right above Manhattan.

fact.label: Look up!
fact.text: With zero light pollution, you could see the Milky Way from city streets.

scenes.narration: Every winter, water seeps into cracks in the roads, freezes and expands. The cracks grow bigger, and seeds blown in by the wind take root.
Within a few decades, many houses would collapse, and whole streets would start turning into forest.
After a few hundred years, even our great steel bridges would rust and fall. But here is the strangest part.
Giant carvings in hard granite, like the faces on Mount Rushmore, could last for millions of years. Long after everything else we built has crumbled away.

fact.label: The last survivors
fact.text: Granite carvings like Mount Rushmore could last millions of years.

scenes.narration: So, a quick recap. Hours: darkness. Days: flooded tunnels. Decades: forests. And millions of years later, a few stone faces. Subscribe, and next time, Sir Digsworth digs even deeper.
